paragraphs: [Tosefta Bava Metzia, chapter 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Bava_Metzia.6.6), mentions him saying, “Anyone who has money and does not lend it at interest,” etc. The Babylonian Talmud, Bava Metzia 76a as cited here (the parallel is at [71a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.71a.6)), reads Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.[^3]
[Yoma 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.53b.3) says, “They said in the name of Shemayah”; Dikdukei Soferim reads “in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai.”
Pirkei deRabbi Eliezer, chapter 15, also has “Rabbi Shemayah says,” etc.

notes.text: The notice preserves the explicit not-lending-at-interest wording and its Shimon ben Elazar attribution. The other citation gives Shemayah versus Shimon ben Yochai.
The consulted Yoma 53b reads “in the name of Shemayah.” The other citations and the Dikdukei Soferim reading are reported here from Hyman.

The Tosefta names Shemayah and speaks of someone who does not lend at interest. The Bavli parallel names Shimon ben Elazar and describes someone who lends without charging interest. Yoma attributes its separate teaching on how to conclude the prayer to Shemayah. The Dikdukei Soferim reading and Pirkei deRabbi Eliezer citation remain as reported by Hyman.
